newsitem.title: JAPAN: Jusco says unclear if arrested chief will resign.
newsitem.headline: Jusco says unclear if arrested chief will resign.

text.p: Japanese supermarket chain Jusco Co Ltd said on Wednesday that it did not yet know whether its president Kenji Tanaka, who was arrested on Tuesday in connection with a racketeer scandal, would resign.
The company said it may hold a news conference later on Wednesday, but that it was unclear whether Tanaka would step down.
Tanaka is a former managing director of Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) and he was arrested on suspicion of involvement in the scandal over loans and payoffs to a racketeer.
Jusco is considering holding a news conference to be attended by its chairman Takuya Okada later on Wednesday to comment on the arrest, a company spokesman said.
Jusco would aim to start the news conference between 10.30 p.m. and 11.00 p.m. (1300 GMT and 1400 GMT) as Okada is currently in Hong Kong, the spokesman said.
Prosecutors on Tuesday arrested four former DKB officials, including Tanaka, on suspicion of making payoffs in the form of illicit loans to a "sokaiya" racketeer, in violation of the Commercial Code.
Prosecutors said 39 separate loans, totalling 8.8 billion yen, were believed to have been made through Daiwa Shinyo, a non-bank financial firm affiliated with DKB.
Prosecutors also raided Jusco's offices on Wednesday in connection with the scandal.
